report_name: Ukrainian Conti Ransomware Developer Sentenced to 4 Years in US Prison

threat_actors.name: Conti
threat_actors.description: A highly organized, financially motivated cybercriminal enterprise that operated a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model from 2020 to 2022. The group was responsible for over 1,000 attacks globally, using double extortion tactics to extort over $150 million from victims.

threat_actors.name: Oleksii Oleksiyovych Lytvynenko
threat_actors.description: A 44-year-old Ukrainian national who acted as a developer and 'intruder' for the Conti ransomware group between 2020 and 2022. He was personally responsible for compromising at least 12 companies and developing malware for the group. He was sentenced to four years in a U.S. prison.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Conti affiliates gained initial access by exploiting unpatched public-facing applications, such as those from Fortinet and VMware.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Conti affiliates used various methods for initial access, including spearphishing.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: Conti operators used PowerShell for execution and persistence once inside a victim network.

attack_patterns.name: Create Account: Local Account
attack_patterns.description: Conti operators created local accounts to maintain persistence on compromised systems.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
attack_patterns.description: The Conti group used tools like PsExec to move laterally through victim networks via SMB/Windows Admin Shares.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Conti ransomware payload was deployed across victim networks to encrypt files as the primary impact of the attack.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: As part of their double extortion tactic, Conti operators exfiltrated sensitive victim data to their own servers before encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Conti ransomware operators frequently used commands like 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet' to delete Volume Shadow Copies, preventing easy recovery of encrypted files.

malware.name: Conti
malware.description: A ransomware payload deployed by the Conti group to encrypt victim files. It was a key component of their double-extortion RaaS operation.

malware.name: TrickBot
malware.description: A backdoor deployed by Conti operators for command and control and to maintain persistence within a compromised network.

tools.name: Cobalt Strike
tools.description: Used by the Conti group for command and control and to maintain persistence in victim networks.

tools.name: PsExec
tools.description: Used by the Conti group for lateral movement within compromised networks.

tools.name: Mimikatz
tools.description: Used by the Conti group to harvest credentials from compromised systems.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2020-1472
vulnerabilities.description: The Conti group was known to exploit vulnerabilities like ZeroLogon for lateral movement.

identities.name: Critical Infrastructure
identities.description: A class of victims targeted by the Conti ransomware operation.

identities.name: Hospitals
identities.description: A class of victims targeted by the Conti ransomware operation, demonstrating a disregard for public safety.

infrastructure.name: Conti Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A data leak site used by the Conti group to publish stolen data from victims who refused to pay the ransom, as part of their double extortion strategy.

indicators.name: Conti Ransomware DLL Execution via Rundll32
indicators.pattern:
title: Conti Ransomware DLL Execution via Rundll32
id: 4a5b6c7d-8e9f-4a1b-2c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of rundll32.exe, a known TTP for Conti, to execute malicious DLLs. Monitor for unusual parent processes spawning rundll32.exe.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-12
references:
  - https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/ukrainian-national-sentenced-four-years-prison-wire-fraud-conspiracy-connection-conti
tags:
  - attack.t1218.011
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  filter_legit_parents:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\svchost.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_parents
indicators.description: Detects the execution of `rundll32.exe`, which Conti was known to use for executing its malicious DLLs. The detection should focus on instances where `rundll32.exe` is spawned by an unusual parent process.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware like Conti to inhibit system recovery.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-12
references:
  - https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/ukrainian-national-sentenced-four-years-prison-wire-fraud-conspiracy-connection-conti
tags:
  - attack.t1490
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet`, a command frequently used by Conti and other ransomware groups to prevent easy file recovery.

relationships.target_name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
